Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "lowercase rough request for a prompt about the ventilation check at Alder Street Community Workshop. can you turn this into a clear prompt for a model that will prepare a practical inspection plan, not carry out the inspection or claim what the results will be. the check is booked for 14 May 2026, 8 to 11 in the morning, at 18 Alder Street. it is a shared woodworking and repair workshop, about 2,100 square feet, and there may be 12 people working in it during the check. the board wants to understand whether the existing extraction and general air movement are working as expected, and what information still needs to be gathered. this is a planning request, not a request for legal certification or a final safety verdict.

The room has a 3.4 metre ceiling and is split in daily use into the receiving area, the long central bench, the sanding corner, the finishing bay and the small tool room. A portable shop vacuum is used at the central bench for occasional repairs. There are two wall-mounted extraction arms, one on each side of the sanding corner; staff say they move the arm between machines rather than running both machines together. The general exhaust fan is marked EF-2 and is above the rear door. There are also two high windows on the north wall. One opens; the other is painted shut. The loading door is on the west side and is normally open for deliveries between 8 and 9, but it is usually closed for the rest of the morning. Please keep these details separate rather than treating all the openings or equipment as interchangeable.

The manager has a folder with a simple room sketch, a fan service sheet, three weeks of maintenance notes, and a copy of last autumn’s staff survey. The sketch puts the intake grille at the east end and marks the two extraction arms, though it does not show the exact distance from each arm to each sander. The fan service sheet lists EF-2 as a 230-volt unit, with a label stating 1,450 cubic metres per hour; there is no date beside that label and no recent measured airflow value. One maintenance entry says a contractor cleaned the rear grille in February. Another says the north window latch is stiff. Do not turn either entry into evidence that airflow is adequate or inadequate.

Keep these reported remarks exactly as written in the prompt and use them as reported observations, not verified findings: the sanding lead said, "The west bench smells strongest after lunch." A regular volunteer said, "When both doors are shut, the paper by the intake barely moves." The workshop coordinator said, "We open the loading door for deliveries, but not as a fix for the whole day." The notes do not say which day or which machine was in use when those remarks were made, so the plan should not assign them a more precise time or cause. Also retain this service note exactly: "Fan EF-2 belt replaced on 6 May; tension not recorded." It is a record of maintenance, not a measurement.

Access and timing are a bit awkward. The building manager can escort a contractor to the roof hatch from 8 until noon only; roof access is needed to see the outdoor termination, and no one should assume the contractor can go up alone. The workshop can provide one employee to demonstrate the usual sanding setup, but that person is not available until 9:30. The electrician is on site from 8:30 to 10:00 and can identify the fan switch and isolator, but is not being asked to open or repair the fan. The board has asked for a plan that fits the booked 8 to 11 visit and says who needs to be present for each part. If the contractor can only attend after 3pm, the manager cannot escort roof access that day; the prompt should ask for a separate contingency in that case, and must not suggest that outdoor termination inspection or airflow readings can still be completed from the roof. Do not quietly ignore this condition just because the booked time is in the morning.

Some more limits from the board: no drilling, cutting, opening ductwork, moving fixed machinery, or interrupting the shared electrical supply during this visit. It is fine to observe normal work, take notes, photograph accessible labels and visible components with permission, and take non-invasive measurements if the contractor brings suitable instruments. Ask the model to distinguish what can be checked visually from what would need an instrument or another visit. The board has not supplied an airflow target, exposure limit, instrument list, or applicable standard. The plan should identify these as missing information where relevant; it should not invent values, claim compliance, or state that the workshop is safe or unsafe. It should also avoid assuming that the survey or quoted remarks represent everyone’s experience.

Provide a short purpose, preparation steps and materials to review, a time-ordered sequence for the 8–11 visit, and a clear record of what to note in each area. Include these points as a numbered section and keep them distinct:
